title: Print a plugin's next-step note after enable
head: b98fce59962b
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: The Setup > Plugins > Enable path discards the next-step note
leads.consequence: Selecting Enable Plugin in the shipped menu runs the CLI in a detached bash process, not in a terminal; the new note goes to process stdout rather than to the user. The Add menu action explicitly opens a floating terminal, but Enable does not. Plugins requiring a follow-up click or command give no visible guidance on this existing user path. Display a notice or launch/present the enable command in a terminal when a note is present.
leads.triage: already_in_opus_final; menu Enable detached; optional note

leads.summary: Duplicate manifest IDs can print instructions for a different plugin than the one the shell enabled
leads.consequence: When two hand-installed user plugin directories claim the same id, the shell's scan assigns the later manifest to installedPlugins[id], while the catalog's unique_by(.id) retains the first manifest. The new note prints the first directory's postEnable even though the shell enabled the second directory. This can direct the user to run the wrong installer or setup command; use the shell's resolved manifest or align catalog precedence with its scan. This is confirmed at the pinned head and current quattro; open #12872 proposes changing precedence and needs re-evaluation if it merges first.
leads.triage: confirmed_by_opus_followup; duplicate IDs: inherited from base catalog-based bar checks, hand-made duplicates only; opus/followup-1-duplicate-ids.md; kept in REPORT.md

leads.summary: An unrelated malformed manifest can silently suppress the note after successful enable
leads.consequence: The catalog feeds every discovered JSON manifest to one jq invocation. A separate malformed user manifest makes it fail, while the shell parses each independently and can still enable a valid plugin. The new `|| return 0` swallows failure, prints only Enabled and exposes jq error(s) on stderr. With no placement, one prior catalog call also errors, hence two stderr lines in the reproducer. Read the resolved manifest via the shell or isolate bad catalog entries, and avoid claiming success without its promised note.
leads.triage: already_in_opus_final; catalog failure absorbed by || return 0; pre-existing catalog behaviour; low value

leads.summary: ASCII-only filtering and pre-filter length cap erase non-English next steps
leads.consequence: A Unicode note loses every non-ASCII character rather than only control bytes. With a 2,000-character accented prefix followed by `NEXT STEP`, the character-based cap slices away the step first, then the byte filter removes the entire prefix, leaving no note and status 0. Normal plugin guidance in other languages also becomes unreadable. Strip terminal controls while preserving valid UTF-8, and cap the actual displayed text.

leads.summary: Carriage return survives the alleged control-byte filter; NUL values warn on stderr
leads.consequence: `tr -cd '\11\12\15\40-\176'` deliberately retains CR (octal 15), so a manifest note can return the cursor to the start of its displayed line even though docs say control bytes are stripped. A JSON NUL reaches Bash command substitution before the filter and produces an ignored-null-byte warning on stderr, despite otherwise succeeding. Remove carriage returns from terminal output and filter control data before it reaches a command substitution that warns.
leads.triage: already_in_opus_final; CR part in F1; NUL warning in Details Verified

leads.summary: The plugin validator accepts malformed postEnable values that enable silently discards
leads.consequence: A plugin manifest with `postEnable` as an object passes `omarchy plugin validate`, then can be added/updated successfully because both paths call that validator, yet the new output code ignores the value without diagnosing it. This defeats validation as a plugin author's pre-publication check for the newly documented string field. Reject non-string postEnable when present, or explicitly document the silent-ignore behavior and add coverage.

leads.summary: The shell README edit cannot merge onto current quattro's relocated docs
leads.location: shell/README.md:100 at PR head; shell/README.md:1-9 at current quattro
leads.consequence: Current quattro replaced the 300-line shell README with a nine-line link hub, and points readers at docs/omarchy-shell.md as the canonical reference. A three-way merge of this PR's README addition with intake tip 8b4eae66 produces a content conflict (markers at lines 5/303/309). Drop the old README hunk during rebase; the already-changed docs/omarchy-shell.md is the correct canonical location. Also ensure the manual link points to the canonical reference, as current quattro already does.

leads.summary: The new test would pass even if the terminal-byte sanitization were removed
leads.consequence: The fixture contains no ESC character at all, so `[[ $hint_out != *$'\033'* ]]` is a vacuous safety assertion. Removing the entire `tr -cd ...` filter from the actual production enable script leaves the test green, as confirmed by a disposable mutant run. Add real control bytes to postEnable and assert both permitted and forbidden output bytes.

## Automated AI review > **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review. **Outcome:** The `postEnable` filter deletes all non-ASCII text, not only the control bytes the docs mention. ### Non-ASCII `postEnable` text is stripped `tr -cd '\11\12\15\40-\176'` keeps only tab, LF, CR and printable ASCII: `Open Setup › Plugins, then run café-setup` prints as `Open Setup Plugins, then run caf-setup`, and a Japanese note prints nothing. CR survives, so a note can overwrite its own line. **Suggested change:** Filter in jq, e.g. `.postEnable | select(type == "string") | .[0:2000] | gsub("[^\\P{Cc}\\t\\n]"; "")`, which keeps UTF-8 and drops CR, ESC, BEL and NUL.
Reproducer (fails at b98fce5) Reproducer: `postEnable` loses every non-ASCII character (reviewed head b98fce59962b27f272f4dd50e4dd086d3289bd56) Append this case to `test/shell.d/plugin-enable-test.sh` (it reuses the file's `run_enable` helper and `$TMPDIR`): ```bash utf8_dir="$TMPDIR/home/.config/omarchy/plugins/acme.utf8" mkdir -p "$utf8_dir" cat >"$utf8_dir/manifest.json" <<'JSON' { "schemaVersion": 1, "id": "acme.utf8", "name": "UTF-8 hint", "version": "1.0.0", "kinds": ["bar-widget"], "entryPoints": { "barWidget": "Widget.qml" }, "postEnable": "Open Setup › Plugins, then run café-setup" } JSON printf 'import QtQuick\nItem {}\n' >"$utf8_dir/Widget.qml" utf8_out=$(LANG=C.UTF-8 run_enable acme.utf8) [[ $utf8_out == *"Open Setup › Plugins, then run café-setup"* ]] || fail "plugin enable keeps non-ASCII postEnable text" "$utf8_out" pass "plugin enable keeps non-ASCII postEnable text" ``` Run: `LANG=C.UTF-8 bash test/shell.d/plugin-enable-test.sh` Actual output at b98fce5 (exit 1): stdout: ``` ok - plugin enable combines activation and placement in one shell mutation ok - plugin enable forwards relative placement ok - plugin enable leaves default placement to the registry ok - plugin enable rejects placement for full bars ok - plugin enable prints a plugin's postEnable text ``` stderr: ``` Enabled acme.utf8 Open Setup Plugins, then run caf-setup not ok - plugin enable keeps non-ASCII postEnable text ``` Further cases, same head, `LANG=C.UTF-8`, one plugin per value (stdout shown as a Python repr; exit 0 in every case): | `postEnable` (JSON) | stdout | |---|---| | `"Don’t forget → run café-setup ✓"` | `'Enabled acme.utf8\n\nDont forget run caf-setup \n'` | | `"Запустите install-loader"` (Cyrillic "Run install-loader") | `'Enabled acme.cyrillic\n\n install-loader\n'` | | `"設定を開いてください"` (Japanese "Open settings") | `'Enabled acme.japanese\n'` (the note is dropped entirely) | | `"AAAAAAAA\rBB"` | `'Enabled acme.cr\n\nAAAAAAAA\rBB\n'` (carriage return kept) | With the filter done in jq instead (`.postEnable | select(type == "string") | .[0:2000] | gsub("[^\\P{Cc}\\t\\n]"; "")`, jq 1.8.2), the case above passes, the Japanese and Cyrillic notes print unchanged, the carriage return, ESC, BEL, NUL and U+009B are removed, and tab and newline are kept.
### The new test does not cover the filter or the cap Test-only gap: the fixture has no ESC byte, so the `$'\033'` check cannot fail, and the test still passes with the `tr` line or the length cap deleted. Regressions in either would go unnoticed. **Suggested change:** Add ESC/BEL and non-ASCII fixtures and assert on the output.
Reproducer (mutants pass at b98fce5) Reproducer: the new test passes with the byte filter or the length cap removed (reviewed head b98fce59962b27f272f4dd50e4dd086d3289bd56) The fixture's `postEnable` contains no ESC byte (its only control byte is a newline), so the `$'\033'` assertion cannot fail. Mutant 1: delete this line from `print_post_enable` in `bin/omarchy-plugin-enable`: ```bash text=$(LC_ALL=C printf '%s' "$text" | tr -cd '\11\12\15\40-\176') ``` Mutant 2 (separately): delete the length cap: ```bash if (( ${#text} > 2000 )); then text="${text:0:2000}" fi ``` Run: `bash test/shell.d/plugin-enable-test.sh` Actual output for each mutant (exit 0, stderr empty): ``` ok - plugin enable combines activation and placement in one shell mutation ok - plugin enable forwards relative placement ok - plugin enable leaves default placement to the registry ok - plugin enable rejects placement for full bars ok - plugin enable prints a plugin's postEnable text ``` A case that does cover the filter (append to `test/shell.d/plugin-enable-test.sh`): ```bash esc_dir="$TMPDIR/home/.config/omarchy/plugins/acme.esc" mkdir -p "$esc_dir" cat >"$esc_dir/manifest.json" <<'JSON' { "schemaVersion": 1, "id": "acme.esc", "name": "Escape hint", "version": "1.0.0", "kinds": ["bar-widget"], "entryPoints": { "barWidget": "Widget.qml" }, "postEnable": "ESC]0;pwnedBELESC[2JRun install-loader" } JSON # ESC and BEL become the JSON escapes for the escape and bell characters sed -i -e 's/ESC/\\u00''1b/g' -e 's/BEL/\\u00''07/g' "$esc_dir/manifest.json" printf 'import QtQuick\nItem {}\n' >"$esc_dir/Widget.qml" esc_out=$(run_enable acme.esc) [[ $esc_out == *"Run install-loader"* ]] || fail "plugin enable prints the sanitized postEnable text" "$esc_out" [[ $esc_out != *$'\033'* && $esc_out != *$'\a'* ]] || fail "plugin enable strips control bytes from postEnable" "$(printf '%q' "$esc_out")" pass "plugin enable strips control bytes from postEnable" ``` At b98fce5 unchanged it passes (exit 0; last stdout line `ok - plugin enable strips control bytes from postEnable`). With mutant 1 it fails (exit 1). stderr: ``` $'Enabled acme.esc\n\n\E]0;pwned\a\E[2JRun install-loader' not ok - plugin enable strips control bytes from postEnable ```
More findings: shell/README.md hunk conflicts with quattro ### `shell/README.md` hunk conflicts with `quattro` `quattro` cut `shell/README.md` to an index pointing at `docs/omarchy-shell.md`; this hunk is the PR's only conflict. **Suggested change:** Rebase and drop the `shell/README.md` hunk. **Reproducer:** Reproducer: the `shell/README.md` hunk is the PR's conflict with current `quattro` Head b98fce59962b27f272f4dd50e4dd086d3289bd56, `quattro` at 8b4eae66da2938ba9559f103b18dbf85cdf28a70 (git 2.55.0): ``` $ git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only --no-messages b98fce59962b27f272f4dd50e4dd086d3289bd56 8b4eae66da2938ba9559f103b18dbf85cdf28a70 02e285ebf06724cab69fbd6e144f8d903d78d55b shell/README.md ``` Exit status 1. Without `--no-messages` the messages are: ``` Auto-merging docs/omarchy-shell.md Auto-merging shell/README.md CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in shell/README.md ``` On `quattro`, b094787f ("Point shell documentation to the canonical reference") cut `shell/README.md` down to a nine-line index that links to `docs/omarchy-shell.md` as the shell reference, so the paragraph the PR edits there no longer exists. Details **Verified:** - The note prints after `Enabled`, `Enabled and moved` and `Now using … as the bar`, and after `omarchy plugin add --enable`. - Missing, `null`, empty and non-string values give output identical to the base script. - ESC, BEL and U+009B are removed (NUL is dropped too, with a bash warning on stderr); 5000 characters are cut to 2000. - Exit status stays 0, including when the plugin catalog fails. - The PR's test fails against the base script and passes at the head and on current `quattro`. **Optional notes:** - Setup › Plugins › Enable runs `omarchy-menu-plugin enable` detached, without a terminal, so the note is not shown there (source reading only). A notification or a docs mention would cover menu users. - `omarchy-plugin-validate` does not check `postEnable`; an array or object value is silently ignored at enable time. A type check would surface the mistake. - Open #10171 also appends to `test/shell.d/plugin-enable-test.sh`; keeping both blocks resolves that conflict.
